title: Extensionality of list search
statement: Let $\alpha$ be a type, let $xs$ be a list of elements of $\alpha$, and let $p,q:\alpha\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be predicates that agree on every element of $xs$. Then the optional first element of $xs$ satisfying $p$ equals the optional first element satisfying $q$.
hypotheses_covered: $xs$ is a list of elements of $\alpha$
$p$ and $q$ agree on every member of $xs$
replaced:
If two Boolean predicates agree on every member of a list, then searching the
list for the first element satisfying the one returns the same result as
searching for the first element satisfying the other.
